Since all the ABLAPLs relate to the same FIR, on the consent of the parties, they are taken up together and are disposed of by this common order.

2. Heard learned counsel for the Petitioners and learned counsel for the State.
3.
The Petitioners are seeking pre-arrest bail in connection with G.R. Case No.92 of 2025 pending in Ramesh Chandra Rout vs State Of Odisha ....

1
the Court of learned J.M.F.C., Tarva, arising out of Tarva P.S. Case No.95 of 2025 for commission of offence punishable under Sections 419/420/34 of IPC.

4. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the Petitioners that even if the allegations are accepted at its face value of accepting money for providing jobs, custodial interrogation of the Petitioners is not warranted.
Hence, the Petitioners may be protected by pre-arrest bail.

5. Learned counsel for the State opposes such prayer and also stated, on instruction, which is taken on record that the Petitioners did not appear before the I.O. on 28.07.2025 in terms of the direction of this Court.
6. Learned counsel for the Petitioners refutes such submission.
7. This Court ignores the submission of the learned counsel for the State regarding the non- appearance in view of the submission of the learned counsel for the Petitioners.

8. Taking into account the nature of allegations of accepting money for providing jobs and its societal ramifications and the money trail to the account of the Petitioners in ABLAPL Nos.8055 of 2025 and 8072 of 2025 at the behest of Petitioner in ABLAPL No.8053 of 2025, as borne out from the case diary, this Court is not inclined to entertain these applications for pre-arrest bail.

However,
in the event the Petitioners surrender before the learned Court in seisin in the aforesaid case and moves an application for their release on bail, the same shall be considered on its own merit.
9. Accordingly, the ABLAPLs stand disposed of.
10. U.C.C. as per rules.
(V. NARASINGH) Judge Santoshi Location: High Court of Orissa, Cuttack Ramesh Chandra Rout vs State Of Odisha ....
